easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:1 says, “A wise son heareth his father’s instruction.”
easy.q: What does a wise son hear?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth.”
easy.q: What does a man eat by the fruit of his mouth?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:3 says, “He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life.”
easy.q: What does the person who keeps his mouth keep?

answers: The sluggard desires and has nothing, but the diligent is made fat
The sluggard is satisfied, but the diligent has nothing
medium.explanation: The sluggard desires without possessing, while the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the sluggard and the diligent person?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 13:3 warns that he who opens his lips wide “shall have destruction.”
medium.q: What happens to the person who opens his lips wide?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 13:5 says, “A righteous man hateth lying.”
medium.q: What does a righteous man hate?

answers: Speech can bring good or destruction
Speech has no effect on life
Only wealth determines a person’s future
challenge.explanation: Good speech brings good, while careless or excessive speech can bring destruction.
challenge.q: What relationship between speech and consequences is shown in these verses?

answers: Hearing instruction is contrasted with hating lying
The wise are contrasted with the diligent
challenge.explanation: Verse 1 commends receiving instruction, while verse 5 describes the righteous person’s hatred of lying.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between verses 1 and 5?

challenge.explanation: Each is characterized by restraint, obedience, or faithful effort rather than foolishness.
challenge.q: What quality is shared by the wise son, the person who keeps his mouth, and the diligent?

answers: It keeps him in the way
easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:6 says, “Righteousness keepeth him that is upright in the way.”
easy.q: What does righteousness do for the upright person?

answers: Some appear rich but have nothing, while others appear poor but have great riches
Everyone who appears rich truly is rich
easy.explanation: The verse contrasts outward appearance with actual possessions.
easy.q: What contrast does verse 7 give about outward wealth?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:9 says, “The light of the righteous rejoiceth.”
easy.q: What happens to the light of the righteous?

medium.explanation: Righteousness keeps the upright, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
medium.q: What is contrasted with righteousness in verse 6?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “The ransom of a man’s life are his riches.”
medium.q: What can serve as a ransom for a man’s life?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 13:10 says, “Only by pride cometh contention.”
medium.q: What does verse 10 say comes only by pride?

answers: Wealth may be only an appearance and is not a complete protection
Wealth belongs only to righteous people
challenge.explanation: Some only appear rich, and riches are described as a ransom rather than an absolute safeguard.
challenge.q: What limitation of wealth appears in verses 7–8?

answers: The righteous rejoice, but the wicked’s lamp is put out
challenge.explanation: The verse places the rejoicing light of the righteous against the extinguished lamp of the wicked.
challenge.q: How do the light and lamp illustrate the difference between the righteous and the wicked?

answers: Prudence and willingness to receive counsel
challenge.explanation: Pride produces contention, while wisdom is found with those who receive good advice.
challenge.q: What quality is encouraged by the contrast between pride and the well-advised?

paragraphs.title: Accumulating Wealth, Hope, and Wise Teaching

easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:11 says, “Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished.”
easy.q: What happens to wealth gotten by vanity?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Hope deferred maketh the heart sick.”
easy.q: What does deferred hope make the heart?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:14 calls it “a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.”
easy.q: What is the law of the wise?

medium.explanation: The verse contrasts diminished wealth with wealth gathered by labour, which shall increase.
medium.q: What is the advantage of gathering wealth by labour?

answers: Hope that has already been fulfilled
medium.explanation: The phrase describes hope whose fulfillment is delayed.
Proverbs 13:13 says, “he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.”
medium.q: What happens to the person who fears the commandment?

answers: The pain of delayed hope contrasts with the blessing of fulfilled desire and obedience
challenge.explanation: Deferred hope makes the heart sick, while fulfilled desire is a tree of life and reverence for the commandment is rewarded.
challenge.q: What emotional contrast appears between verses 12 and 13?

answers: It helps him depart from the snares of death
challenge.explanation: It is a fountain of life that leads a person away from deadly snares.
challenge.q: How does the law of the wise help a person?

answers: Patient labor, hope, obedience, wisdom, and turning from danger
challenge.explanation: The verses connect responsible labor and hope with obedience, wise teaching, and escape from evil.
challenge.q: What progression is found in verses 11–15?

paragraphs.title: Conduct, Messengers, and the Company of the Wise

easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:16 says, “Every prudent man dealeth with knowledge.”
easy.q: How does every prudent man deal?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “a faithful ambassador is health.”
Proverbs 13:20 says, “He that walketh with wise men shall be wise.”
easy.q: With whom shall a person become wise?

answers: The prudent deals with knowledge, but the fool lays open his folly
The fool deals with knowledge, but the prudent reveals folly
medium.explanation: Verse 16 contrasts knowledgeable conduct with openly displayed folly.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the prudent man and the fool?

medium.explanation: An ambassador is a messenger or representative sent with a message.
medium.q: What is an ambassador in the context of verse 17?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 13:17 says, “A wicked messenger falleth into mischief.”
medium.q: What happens to a wicked messenger?

answers: The character of a messenger affects the result of his mission
Every messenger produces the same result
challenge.explanation: The wicked messenger falls into mischief, while the faithful ambassador brings health.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the wicked messenger and the faithful ambassador teach?

answers: Accepting correction and walking with the wise bring honor and wisdom, while foolish company causes harm
They deny that companions influence anyone
challenge.explanation: Refusing instruction brings poverty and shame, while wise companions promote wisdom.

answers: Deal with knowledge, accept reproof, and walk with wise people
Reject instruction and keep foolish company
challenge.explanation: The passage commends prudent conduct, regard for reproof, and fellowship with the wise.
challenge.q: Which choice best follows the teaching of these verses?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.”
easy.q: To whom is the wealth of the sinner laid up?

answers: To the satisfying of his soul
easy.explanation: Proverbs 13:25 says, “The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul.”
easy.q: What does the righteous person eat?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 13:22 says, “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children.”
medium.q: What does a good man leave to his children’s children?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 13:24 says, “He that spareth his rod hateth his son.”
medium.q: What does a person who spares his rod do according to the verse?

answers: The righteous is satisfied, but the wicked lacks
The righteous lacks, but the wicked is satisfied
medium.explanation: The righteous eat to the satisfying of his soul, while the belly of the wicked shall want.
medium.q: What is the contrast at the end of the chapter?

answers: Goodness is passed to future generations, while loving discipline guides children
Family and discipline have no connection
Both verses discuss only personal wealth
challenge.explanation: The passage speaks of leaving an inheritance and of correcting a son in love.
challenge.q: How do inheritance and discipline relate in verses 22–24?

answers: The poor may have much food in the tillage, while the wicked still lacks satisfaction
The poor always lack food, while the wicked is satisfied
Both verses say that food is unimportant
challenge.explanation: The verses distinguish available provision from the lack of judgment and the wicked person’s continuing want.
challenge.q: What contrast between verses 23 and 25 concerns provision?

answers: Conduct, discipline, and righteousness affect present life and future generations
Wealth is the only goal of life
challenge.explanation: The verses connect moral conduct, inheritance, correction, provision, and satisfaction.
challenge.q: What principle summarizes this final group of verses?
